A – Peter Beck / Adam Spice:

- The mix depends heavily on customer program schedules and payload readiness.

- Management indicated approximately 15 HASTE missions are currently contemplated.

- Adam Spice estimated HASTE could represent approximately 25% of total small dedicated launches in 2027.

- The actual mix could fluctuate depending on customer readiness.

discussion_digest: The biggest story today is NVIDIA (NVDA), which exploded to 1,232 Reddit mentions, more than double yesterday's 553. While it remains the top ticker, Stocktwits sentiment is dead even at 16 bullish and 16 bearish. Some users are bearish, with one saying 'come on buy more and drop more... another 10% down... $160 I'm waiting for you,' while others dismiss lawsuits as a 'nothing burger.' This split shows a battle between dip buyers and those expecting a pullback, making NVDA the most contentious stock of the day.

Other notable discussions include a surge in AMD mentions (230, up from 64) with very bullish Stocktwits sentiment (21 bullish vs 4 bearish). Users are calling for a short squeeze, with one saying 'shorts about to get pulverized.' The Trade Desk (TTD) also spiked from 1 to 40 mentions and is trending on Yahoo Finance; bulls are defending the stock after earnings, citing $200 million EBITDA, a $150 million revenue beat, and a $700 million buyback, while the stock price seems to have dropped. AST SpaceMobile (ASTS) and Rocket Lab (RKLB) are also hot, with users hyping launch contracts and calling RKLB a 'generational company.'

The crowd disagrees most on NVDA, where bullish and bearish tags are evenly split, and on GOOGL, which saw a massive mention increase but has some technical resistance warnings. This tension suggests uncertainty; while many are bullish on tech overall, there's a growing contingent expecting a pullback. For regular investors, it's a reminder that high attention doesn't always mean unanimous optimism, and it's wise to consider both sides before jumping in.

overlooked_insights.title: Anthropic IPO cornerstone investors revealed
overlooked_insights.insight: Users are circulating details from Anthropic's S-1: Google, Nvidia, AMD, Broadcom, Micron, Microsoft, and TSMC will invest $26 billion via private placement at the IPO price, and cornerstone investors will sell 23,333,331 shares in the IPO. Anthropic aims to raise up to $69.3 billion. This is a massive capital reallocation event that ties the AI chip complex to a single liquidity event.
overlooked_insights.evidence: One user posts: 'ANTHROPIC SAYS $GOOGL, $NVDA, $AMD, BROADCOM, $MU, MICROSOFT, TSMC TO INVEST $26 BLN THROUGH PRIVATE PLACEMENT AT IPO PRICE' and 'CORNERSTONE INVESTORS WILL SELL 23,333,331 SHARES IN THE IPO'.
overlooked_insights.why_overlooked: Mainstream headlines mention Anthropic's data center footprint but not the specific cornerstone investor list, share counts, or the $69.3B raise target.

overlooked_insights.title: Google TPU 8tx/8i Max specs leak
overlooked_insights.insight: Users describe Google's new TPU 8tx and 8i Max chips: the 8tx targets secure, hardware-enforced confidential computing and uses AMD 5th Gen EPYC processors as host CPUs, while the 8i Max is a specialized inference chip. This is a direct challenge to Nvidia's dominance and explains AMD's Google Cloud win.
overlooked_insights.evidence: One user writes: 'Google is expanding its AI chip lineup with two new specialized versions of its Tensor Processing Units (TPUs), the TPU 8tx and 8i Max' and another: 'AMD's 5th Gen EPYC processors power the host CPUs for Google Cloud's TPU 8tx system. First cloud TPU with hardware-enforced confidential computing'.
overlooked_insights.why_overlooked: Mainstream coverage mentions AMD's Google Cloud chip selection but not the specific TPU model names, the confidential computing feature, or the AMD EPYC host CPU detail.

overlooked_insights.title: Senate energy permitting bill advances 73-25
overlooked_insights.insight: Users flag that the US Senate voted 73-25 to invoke cloture on a bipartisan energy permitting bill, which would fast-track critical infrastructure projects including data center power connectivity. One user notes a $35 billion estimated cost for connectivity infrastructure as the only caveat. This is a direct catalyst for data center buildout and pipeline/utility names.
overlooked_insights.evidence: One user quotes: 'Nov 9 (Reuters) - The US Senate voted to advance debate on a sweeping bipartisan energy permitting bill on Monday ... The Senate voted 73-25 to invoke cloture' and another: 'This is huge news.. Everyone is so focused on the Nvidia thing they are not seeing what else is going on. The only minor caveat to this fast tracking bill is a $35 billion estimated cost for connectivity to infrastructure'.
overlooked_insights.why_overlooked: Mainstream headlines focus on Nvidia's CEO scandal and CPI; the Senate cloture vote on energy permitting is buried and not connected to data center power demand.

overlooked_insights.title: DTE-Google Project Cannoli contracts approved
overlooked_insights.insight: Michigan regulators approved DTE's 20-year power contracts for Google's 1-gigawatt data center near Detroit (Project Cannoli) on Thursday, with ratepayer protections including minimum billing demand. This is a concrete, approved data center power deal that directly ties DTE's regulated growth to Google's AI buildout.
overlooked_insights.evidence: One user posts: 'Michigan regulators approved DTE's 20-year power contracts for Google's 1-gigawatt data center near Detroit (Project Cannoli) on Thursday, with the ratepayer protections doing the heavy lifting. Google pays a minimum billing demand'.
overlooked_insights.why_overlooked: Mainstream DTE headlines cover the Vantage sale and analyst price targets but not the specific Project Cannoli regulatory approval or the 1-GW Google contract terms.

NVDA.summary: Nvidia is dominating online discussion right now, with Reddit mentions more than doubling from 553 to 1,232 in the past 24 hours, putting it at the number one rank across all tickers tracked. The conversation is intense and polarized, driven largely by a swirl of rumors and news about CEO Jensen Huang—specifically chatter about an alleged affair and vague claims about a Chinese operation or espionage angle. Some posters are convinced this is a coordinated smear campaign by short sellers and foreign actors trying to tank the stock, while others are treating the negative headlines as a reason to expect further downside. On Stocktwits, bullish and bearish tags are dead even at 16 apiece, which tells you the crowd is genuinely split. You'll see a lot of conspiracy-minded posts claiming the FBI will investigate shorts and Chinese operatives, alongside bearish calls for the stock to drop to $135 or $160. There's also a camp that thinks the whole thing is a 'nothing burger'—pointing out that big tech companies get sued all the time and Nvidia has unlimited resources to fight back. The bulls are eyeing $300+ if Jensen is cleared and earnings beat expectations. The bears are mocking anyone buying the dip and predicting another 10% drop. What investors should know: this is a classic case of headline risk overwhelming fundamentals in the short term. The stock is reacting to rumor and speculation rather than confirmed financial news, and the community is extremely reactive. The even split on Stocktwits suggests no clear consensus, which often means volatility ahead. If you're holding NVDA, expect choppy price action until there's clarity on the Huang situation and the next earnings report. The Reddit mention surge itself is a signal of heightened retail attention, which can amplify moves in either direction. Don't get caught up in the conspiracy theories—focus on the actual business fundamentals, which remain strong, but be aware that sentiment is fragile and the stock could swing hard on any new development. The key takeaway is that the online community is treating this as a binary event: either the allegations blow over and the stock rips, or they gain traction and it sells off further. Position sizing and risk management matter more than ever here.

Another pointed out that the bill has a $35 billion estimated cost for connectivity infrastructure spread over 10 years, but they still see it as a positive catalyst. There's also talk about buybacks being massive, which could support the stock price. On the price action, some investors are saying the floor has been reached and the journey up has begun, urging patience. Others prefer a gradual, steady climb over crazy swings, with one mentioning $800 as solid ground to buy more if it dips. However, not everyone is convinced—one message calls it a 'complete fakeout and pump,' though ironically tagged as bullish. Overall, the community seems to believe the worst is over and that the stock is poised for recovery, driven by infrastructure spending and data center demand. Investors should note that while sentiment is very positive, the stock may still be volatile, and the bill's actual impact could take time to materialize. It's also worth watching whether the bullish enthusiasm translates into sustained buying or if it's just short-term hype.

ET.summary: Energy Transfer (ET) is buzzing in online communities, with Reddit mentions nearly tripling from 15 to 49 in the last 24 hours, landing it at rank 12. On Stocktwits, the sentiment is heavily bullish—26 bullish tags compared to only 2 bearish. The discussion is dominated by income investors who love ET's high dividend yield, which is nearly 7%. Many users are buying the dip, especially after the stock price fell to the mid-$18 range. One investor said they bought every share they could in the mid-18s, calling the dividend and upside potential a no-brainer. Another mentioned adding on the ex-dividend day, believing ET will do fine with the new 'blue Congress' and that production levels will need to meet demand. There's also a strong belief that data centers will be built somewhere and will require more pipeline infrastructure, which benefits ET. A Citi analyst raised the price target to $25 from $24 on November 6, maintaining a Buy rating, which added to the optimism. Some long-term investors are shrugging off political worries, noting that ET has slowly gone up for years regardless of who is in office. They advise others to calm down and see the sell-off as an opportunity to buy more cheapies. The dividend is a central theme—one user said they don't care if the stock goes to $18 or below because they're here for the $0.35 quarterly dividend. However, there are a few cautious voices. Some worry about the impact of a new Congress on energy policy, but most dismiss those concerns. Overall, the community sees ET as a reliable income play with upside from data center demand and pipeline expansion. Investors should know that while the dividend is attractive, the stock can be sensitive to energy prices and political developments, but the long-term trend has been positive.

TTD.summary: The Trade Desk (TTD) is suddenly one of the hottest topics on Reddit and Stocktwits, with mentions exploding from just 1 to 40 in 24 hours and a Reddit rank of 16. The buzz centers on the company's latest earnings report, which posters say beat revenue expectations by $150 million, delivered roughly $200 million in EBITDA, and came alongside a massive $1 billion share buyback authorization. Bulls are also pointing to 83 million shares sold short and arguing that the after-hours sell-off from $19 back to $15 was driven by short sellers in thin volume rather than real selling. The tone is aggressive and confident—one popular post asks why anyone would worry about the stock price after such a report, calling it a clear buy in the teens. Another says the buyback represents about 15% of market cap and tells followers to 'buckle up for a ride to the moon.' Options traders are chiming in about heavy volume in weekly $18 calls, suggesting some expect a quick rebound. Sentiment tags show 18 bullish versus only 5 bearish, reinforcing the optimistic tilt. However, not everyone is convinced: some messages simply say 'Bears overnight' or note that the stock still fell after earnings, implying skepticism about the rally's durability. The community is clearly frustrated with short sellers and believes the drop was manipulated. Investors should know that the fundamentals cited—strong revenue beat, profitability, and a large buyback—are real positives, but the stock's reaction shows the market may be focused on guidance or other concerns. The heavy short interest cuts both ways: it could fuel a squeeze, but it also reflects genuine bearish bets. The intense retail enthusiasm and talk of 'moons' are classic signs of a potential squeeze setup, but also of hype that can reverse quickly. For a balanced view, watch whether the buyback actually supports the price and whether the next quarter confirms the momentum. The community is overwhelmingly bullish, but the stock's post-earnings drop is a reminder that even good numbers can be priced in.

HIMS.summary: Hims & Hers Health (HIMS) is generating solid chatter on Reddit and Stocktwits, with mentions rising from 4 to 17 in 24 hours and a Reddit rank of 32. The discussion is largely bullish, with 25 bullish tags versus 8 bearish, and posters are excited about two main catalysts: the addition of Dr. Andrew Huberman to the board and a new partnership with Eli Lilly to sell obesity drugs directly on the Hims platform. One popular post calls Huberman a potential game-changer that could turn Hims into a 'health juggernaut,' while another highlights the Lilly deal as a major revenue opportunity. Bulls are also pointing to the company's revenue growth—nearly $140 million more than last quarter—and arguing that the recent 15% sell-off is overdone. One message notes the market cap is down to $5 billion, calling it 'ridiculously low' and predicting a bounce. Another says the post-earnings move down already happened during market hours, so now it only goes up. However, there are cautious voices: one poster says they wouldn't buy until the $15-20 area, implying the stock could fall further. The overall tone is optimistic but with some acknowledgment of volatility. Investors should know that the Huberman board addition brings credibility in the wellness space, and the Lilly partnership could significantly expand Hims' offerings in the lucrative obesity market. However, the stock's negative reaction to earnings suggests the market may be concerned about margins, competition, or integration risks. The community is focused on the long-term potential, but short-term traders are watching key levels. The mix of hype and fundamental developments makes HIMS a stock to watch, but the sell-off despite good news is a caution flag. As always, retail enthusiasm can amplify moves in both directions.

APPS.summary: Digital Turbine (APPS) is getting a lot of attention on Stocktwits after its latest earnings report, even though Reddit mentions are basically zero. The Stocktwits crowd is leaning bullish, with 15 bullish tags versus 6 bearish ones, but the mood is mixed. People are happy about several things: revenue came in around $179 million, beating expectations by about 7%; adjusted EBITDA jumped 46% year over year; and management raised full-year revenue guidance by $20 million. The company's ODS (On-Device Solutions) segment grew 20% and that growth is accelerating, which was a pleasant surprise for many. They also signed another Tier 1 carrier soon after the Orange deal, which bulls see as proof the business is gaining traction. However, the stock dropped after earnings, and that's where the negativity comes in. Gross margins shrank, and EBITDA was nearly flat, which spooked investors. Some point out that the margin compression is because a less profitable part of the business is growing fast, skewing overall margins down. Others worry about debt and the reality that the turnaround may not be as close as previously thought. The price action was ugly, with too many calls and paper hands getting cleared out. Some traders think the drop was overblown and are buying the dip—one even placed a buy order for 5,000 shares at $8.30. But others are more cautious, saying the market was treating the turnaround as 100% confirmed, and now the ceiling might be lower. Predictions of $20 by year-end are looking shaky. Overall, the community sees a strong quarter with some blemishes, and opinions are split on whether this is a short-term blip or a sign of deeper issues. Investors should note the improving revenue and ODS growth, but also keep an eye on margins and debt.
